title: Computational design of zinc metallohydrolases with RFdiffusion2
summary: RFdiffusion2 designed zinc metallohydrolases from quantum-chemistry-derived active-site geometries. The first round of 96 designs produced an enzyme with catalytic efficiency of 16,000 M-1 s-1, and a second round of 96 yielded three more highly active enzymes, with k/K up to 53,000 M-1 s-1. Crystal structures (PDB 9PYJ, 9PYL) were determined, but the evidence covers one designed enzyme family.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design (Baker lab)

evidence.tested: From 96 designs, the best had kcat/KM of 16,000 M^-1 s^-1; a second round of 96 gave three more active enzymes, up to 53,000 M^-1 s^-1 and kcat up to 1.5 s^-1. The crystal structure of the most active design is very close to the model.
evidence.unknown: Use in practical applications is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: RFdiffusion2 designed zinc metallohydrolases from quantum-chemistry active sites; PLACER and Chai-1 analysed the designs.
